(Recommendation 72D, Int. Code zool. Nomencl.)
Hopkins &
"Although
Rothschild (1956, Cat. Rothschild Coll. Fleas II: 5) remarked that
the holotype concept was accepted by Jordan and Rothschild from the
beginning of their work on fleas, they did not in their earliest papers
{actually in the majority of their publications ] publish any statement or
clear implication that one particular specimen was regarded as the type to
the exclusion of all others, and in consequence some of the specimens we have
listed as holotypes are actually lectotypes. 
In such instances our listing
of specimens as holotypes must be regarded as a selection of lectotypes." -
However, Article 74(c) of the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature
states that "Lectotypes must not be designated collectively by a general
statement; each designation must be made specifically for an individual
nominal species, and must have as its object the definition of that species."
Hence, in our view the authors of the Rothschild Flea Catalogue have not
validly designated lectotypes by listing specimens as holotypes. That prac
tice, moreover, does not indicate whether those listed specimens are in fact 
©
holotypes or lectotypes-
In the present list of primary type-specimens in the British Museum
(Natural History) we have therefore selected lectotypes where necessary.
Our selections are indicated by L*, which is short for "hereby selected by
us as lectotype''; we have chosen as lectotypes the syntypes on slides with
red or purple labels because” those specimens were intended primary types.
Remaining syntypes have al 1 been labelled as paralectotypes; lectallotypes
have also been labelled accordingly.
Hopkins & Rothschild (t-c.: 7) further remarked that "Although specimens
in alcohol which were taken into consideration in the original descriptions
are paratypes, we have not listed them as such because of the great difficulty ..-
of separating closely allied species in unmounted material." -- 
We have now
mounted on slides all pera and paralectotypes and, after examination,
labelled them as such.
NOTES ON THE CATALOGUE :
- The literature reference for each description can be found in the concig,
List of References (p. 51).
- Jordan and Rothschild did not indicate in figure legends whether or not ii:
illustrations were made from type-specimens. 
Hence we compared their publishei
figures against primary type-specimens and in a number of instances we could
link illustrations with such specimens - this is shown in the list by the
addition of (H) or (L) after the figure reference number (i.e., the figure 
ws
drawn from.a Holotype or a Lectotype); when we could not be absolutely sure
about such an attribution we have indicated this with (H+) or (It). Ina
number of cases the original figures (mostly early ones) are not sufficiently
accurate or detailed for them to be linked to a certain specimen.
- The three categories of primary type-specimens are indicated as:
H 
- Holotype indicated in published type data as "type" or "holotype"
Hm - Holotype by monotypy
Ht - Holotype indicated as "type!' in the text of
: 
in-the relevant publication
the description or elsewhere

L* - Lectotype by present designation
No Neotype
- A.type-locality is briefly given as name of country or island followed by
name. of actual locality; fuller particulars of the locality may be found in
the List of Type-localities (p. 55).
- The present name of a number of type-hosts may be found in Host synonymy (p. fi
- The present status of a flea taxon - if different from the original one- 
_

In case of synonymy, the senior
synonym is referred to by its code-number (vide Smit & Wright, 1978, A list of
code numbers of species and Subspecies of Siphonaptera. BMNH).
